title: Official Geek'd Con 2026 Guest Lineup: Who To Meet In Shreveport - NewsBreak
text:
By Greg Atoms ,
2 days ago
Shreveport’s premier pop culture event, Geek’d Con, is officially set to return to the Shreveport Convention Center this summer. The 11th installment of the massive three-day convention will take place in Downtown Shreveport from August 14th through the 16th, 2026.
The event serves as the largest gathering of its kind in North Louisiana , and one of the biggest in the whole state. Geek’d Con offers a weekend of celebrity appearances, professional photo ops, and a massive vendor market. It continues to be the primary destination for fans of film, television, and comic books to gather for a professional convention experience.
Geek’d Con 2026 Guest Lineup The guest list for the 2026 show is already starting to take shape with a mix of legendary comic creators and fan favorite actors. This year’s event will have a ton of amazing guests, and will feature another anniversary celebration. This year, the “Scream” franchise turns 30 years old. To celebrate the Shreveport-influenced franchise, Geek’d Con will be hosting a Scream celebration with the Ghostface actors Max Laferriere (from Scream VI) and Jeff Brockton (from Scream 3) …giving horror fans a rare chance to meet multiple generations of Ghostface performers.
Credit: Comics, Beer & Sci-fi via Youtube/Marvel Comics The comic book artist alley is also stacking up with industry veterans who have shaped the world of Marvel and DC Comics. Legendary inker Joe Rubinstein joins a talented group of creators including Roland Paris, Brian Steward, and Jason Turner . These guests bring decades of experience from iconic titles like Wolverine, The Infinity Gauntlet, and Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles.
Vendor Spaces And Ticket Information Vendor registration for the 2026 event is currently moving forward as the floor plan starts to take shape at the Shreveport Convention Center. Business owners and local artists looking to reach thousands of fans in Downtown Shreveport can find all the application details at ShreveportGeeks.com .
Ticket information and further updates on the celebrity lineup will be released as the show draws closer. Fans should keep an eye on GeekdCon.com for the latest news, schedule updates, and programming details for the August event.
Geek'd Con 2026 Guest Lineup Geek'd Con 2026 will be happening at the Shreveport Convention Center August 14-16, 2026. Guest announcements are happening now! Ticket info coming soon! Be sure to follow our Facebook page and download the Geek'd Con app for all the latest guest announcements, info and everything else you need to know!
Geek'd Con brought to you by Morris & Dewett Injury Lawyers. Photo Credit: Geek'd Con Lee Waddell Lee is famously known as the ORIGINAL Ghostface...performing the iconic character’s movements in the 1996 masterpiece Scream.
Waddell was the first person any of us ever saw portray Ghostface, as he was the man behind the mask for the legendary opening sequence involving Drew Barrymore. He was also responsible for the death of Principal Himbry, played by Henry Winkler, which resulted in one of the best stories in the behind-the-scenes stories in Scream history...but that's Lee's story to tell you about when he comes to Shreveport.
Come meet Lee, along with Scream 2 Ghostface Allen Robinson, Scream 3 Ghostface Jeff Brockton, and Scream 6 Ghostface Max Laferriere in Downtown Shreveport this August Photo Credit: Geek'd Con Allen Robinson Actor and stuntman Allen Robinson took his turn as one of the primary physical performers behind Ghostface Scream 2. He set the tone for the iconic killer right away in the franchise's first sequel. Robinson was responsible for some of the most memorable kills in the movie...including the intense opening theater sequence, and the legendary recording studio chase.
Beyond his Ghostface work in the Scream franchise, his served as the stunt double for Matthew Lillard in the original Scream, and Timothy Olyphant in the sequel.
Outside of Scream, Allen has served as Tom Hanks’ stunt double (including the Oscar-winning Forrest Gump) a total of seven times, and Jim Carrey’s stunt double (Batman Forever as The Riddler) three times, and his extensive career also includes stunt work for Clint Eastwood (The Mule).
Not only will Allen be joinign us this August, but he will be doing in-costume photo ops as Ghostface! Photo Credit: Geek'd Con Jeff Brockton The 30th Anniversary celebration of Scream continues...as we go under the mask again. Please welcome Jeff Brockton!
Actor and stuntman Jeff Brockton took his turn as one of the primary physical performers behind Ghostface in the cult-classic Scream 3.
Brockton was responsible for bringing the iconic killer to life during the film's most intense chase and fight sequences...specifically doubling for the character of Roman Bridger. His work helped define the more aggressive and calculated movements of Ghostface during the Hollywood-centered installment of the franchise..
Not only will Jeff be joinign us this August, but he will be doing in-costume photo ops as Ghostface! Photo Credit: Geek'd Con Max Laferriere This year is the 30th Anniversary of the iconic film Scream. To help us celebrate, we're going under the mask. Please welcome Max Laferriere!
Actor and stuntman Max Laferriere is probably best known as the physical embodiment of Ghostface in the film Scream VI.
Laferriere performed the iconic slasher’s movements throughout the movie...including the legendary bodega and apartment scenes. He joins the legacy of the franchise as one of the most intimidating versions of the character to ever wear the mask.
Not only will Max be joining us this August, but he will be doing in-costume photo ops as Ghostface! Photo Credit: Geek'd Con Joe Rubinstein A true comic book legend is coming to Geek'd Con 2026. Hall of Fame artist, Eisner Award winner, and Guinness World Record holder, Joe Rubinstein is joining us!
Joe is an absolute industry titan. His historic resume includes being the primary inker for the legendary Infinity Gauntlet, and inked Frank Miller's work in the definitive 1982 Wolverine miniseries. Even bigger? Joe is the artist who inked Gambit’s very first in-story appearance in X-Men 266!
He set the world record for inking more pencilers than anyone else in history during his epic 20-year run on The Official Handbook of the Marvel Universe.
Beyond his cosmic Marvel milestones and classic Captain America run, Joe’s pen has touched nearly every corner of the DC universe. He took home an Eisner Award for his incredible Justice League work and has provided defining inks for DC heavy hitters like Batman, Superman, Aquaman, and Green Arrow. Photo Credit: Geek'd Con Roland Paris It just wouldn't be Geek'd Con without our most tenured friend of the show, a man who has been a pillar of the event, and is a fabric of everything we do. Coming back this August is everyone's favorite: Roland Paris!
You can find Roland's art on the cover and in the pages of the biggest names in comic books. We're talking about Marvel artwork for characters like Spider-Man, The Avengers, Daredevil, Guardians of the Galaxy, Iron Man, Captain Marvel, Ms. Marvel, She-Hulk, Spider-Girl, X-Men, Black Panther, Daredevil, and a ton more! Photo Credit: Geek'd Con Jason Turner Jason has built a massive reputation as a prolific variant cover artist, highly sought after by publishers and retailers to create exclusives for various issues. His vibrant artwork has graced the covers of massive top-tier titles, including Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtlesl, Godzilla, and the indie hit Feral.
His incredible comic cover credits go on and on, featuring standout work on Image Comics' The Darkness, Archie Comics: Judgement Day, Archie Meets Jay and Silent Bob, and Evil Ink's My Brother's Blood Machine.
When he isn't crushing it in the visual arts, Jason is also an accomplished musician. He has released several albums and EPs over the years Photo Credit: Geek'd Con Brian Steward An industry veteran, his resume spans comics, magazines, and film. Starting at Heavy Metal, his stunning art has graced iconic publications like Fangoria, Scream: The Horror Magazine, and Delirium. He is best known as the driving force behind Fantasm Media. Under that banner, he served as Editor-In-Chief of KISS: The Official Magazine, working directly with Gene Simmons on photography, illustration, and design!
His incredible work goes beyond KISS. He's produced official art for horror legends like George A. Romero and Sid Haig, touching legendary properties like Night of the Living Dead and The Crazies.
He’s always ready to chat horror, art, and rock, signing one-of-a-kind pieces just for fans. 3
